t:
Section 2008 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 609) is amended—
    (1) in subsection (a)—
        (A) in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking “Grants” and all that follows through “used” and inserting the following: “The Administrator shall permit the recipient of a grant under section 2003 or 2004 to use grant funds”; and 
        (B) in paragraph (10), by inserting “, regardless of whether such analysts are current or new full-time employees or contract employees” after “analysts”; and  
    (2) in subsection (b)—
        (A) by redesignating paragraphs (3) and (4) as paragraphs (4) and (5), respectively; and 
        (B) by inserting after paragraph (2) the following:“(3) Limitations on discretion.—“(A) In general.—With respect to the use of amounts awarded to a grant recipient under section 2003 or 2004 for personnel costs in accordance with paragraph (2) of this subsection, the Administrator may not—“(i) impose a limit on the amount of the award that may be used to pay for personnel, or personnel-related, costs that is higher or lower than the percent limit imposed in paragraph (2)(A); or“(ii) impose any additional limitation on the portion of the funds of a recipient that may be used for a specific type, purpose, or category of personnel, or personnel-related, costs.“(B) Analysts.—If amounts awarded to a grant recipient under section 2003 or 2004 are used for paying salary or benefits of a qualified intelligence analyst under subsection (a)(10), the Administrator shall make such 
amounts available without time limitations placed on the period of time that the analyst can serve under the grant.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that grant recipients, often states and localities, are outside parties interacting with FEMA. But the section only governs how grant funds may be used and limits the Administrator's discretion over personnel costs. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, and grant arrangements are not participation under the definition.
fable.s: The Administrator shall permit the recipient of a grant under section 2003 or 2004 to use grant funds

qwen_block.w: This section amends provisions regarding the use of funds by grant recipients. It specifies how grant money can be spent on personnel costs and analysts. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' This text regulates the administration of grants rather than requiring consultation with outside parties or public input in a decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: The Administrator shall permit the recipient of a grant under section 2003 or 2004 to use grant funds

opus.w: This section only changes how grant recipients under sections 2003 and 2004 may use their funds, and it limits the Administrator's discretion to restrict personnel spending. Outside parties appear only as grant recipients, and the definition excludes grants and benefits. Nothing here requires the Administrator to consult outside parties, take public comment, hold a hearing or issue regulations before making a decision. It also does not give anyone a right to challenge a decision.
opus.s: the Administrator may not—“(i) impose a limit on the amount of the award that may be used to pay for personnel, or personnel-related, costs that is higher or lower than the percent limit imposed in paragraph (2)(A)
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section is about how state and local grant recipients use federal homeland security grant funds, so outside parties are involved. But this concerns grant use, which the definition expressly excludes. It also only limits the Administrator's discretion. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends provisions regarding the use of grant funds by recipients. It specifies that the Administrator must allow recipients to use funds for certain personnel costs and limits the Administrator's ability to impose additional restrictions. This relates to the administration of grants, not to a process where outside parties consult with or participate in federal decision-making. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants from being considered participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Administrator shall permit the recipient of a grant under section 2003 or 2004 to use grant funds
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves "grant recipients" who are outside the federal government.
Resolution: The section describes how grant funds can be used (specifically for personnel costs) and limits the Administrator's discretion in imposing restrictions on those costs. It does not require the grant recipients to consult with the government or participate in a decision-making process; rather, it defines the terms of the grant award itself. Applying for or receiving a grant is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
